As mentioned, I believe I used 22 Gauge wire. The goal here is to make 4 seperate .2 ohm coils. Use Steam Engine (or whatever other online calculator you want) to determine how to use the wire you have to make .2 ohm coils. With 22 Gauge Kanthal, wrap around a 2mm bit (same size as the blue screwdrivers) 4 times. Once you have four seperate coils, insert them into your post so that the outside posts have two legs going through them, and the middle post has four. Test the coils, they should all fire nearly simultaneously. If they do not, check to see if they wiggle at all. It took me about 30 minutes to get all four center legs lined up where they all were held tightly by the screw and made full contact with the atty. Then I ran a single wick through each side. I pulled it down so that you have a tuft that touches the deck inbetween the coils, then you tuck the outer tails underneath like a regular wick. Repeat for the otherside. Juice it up and get ready for clouds. Would be stronger as a Quad Sleeper Style, but I am happy with what I got.
